articles.title: PDF image extraction: PNG conversion changed three reports by under 2%, but a 1-bit scan grew 2.37x
articles.excerpt: Picture a routine solo-dev job. A client sends a folder of scanned PDFs, and the plan is to pull the page images out and archive those, because extraction is supposed to be lossless. Then the output f…
articles.body: Picture a routine solo-dev job. A client sends a folder of scanned PDFs, and the plan is to pull the page images out and archive those, because extraction is supposed to be lossless. Then the output folder weighs more than twice what the PDFs did, and storage is billed by the gigabyte. The usual suspect is the PNG step, since anything that is not a JPEG gets decoded and written as a new PNG. In this run it was mostly innocent: across three real reports, PNG conversion moved the extracted total by less than 2% in either direction. The case that grew was a 1-bit scanned page written as RGBA PNG, at 2.37 times the data stored in the PDF. The scope: an Apple-silicon Mac, one run per file.
articles.author: AsyncMonk

articles.title: AI Can Extrapolate Your Sales Data in Ten Seconds. That Is Not a Forecast.
articles.excerpt: Drop three years of monthly sales into a chat window, ask "forecast next year," and you get a smooth upward curve in ten seconds. Would you sign a purchasing budget against it? Two follow-up questions…
articles.body: Drop three years of monthly sales into a chat window, ask "forecast next year," and you get a smooth upward curve in ten seconds. Would you sign a purchasing budget against it? Two follow-up questions usually end the conversation: If a new regulation lands next March, will that curve tell you in advance? No. Can you explain how the curve was produced? Usually not — which means when it drifts, you can only say "it was wrong" after the fact. If you can't answer those, the missing piece isn't a better model. It's the boundary around what you're asking for. Extrapolation is arithmetic. Forecasting is judgment. Most of what people call "AI forecasting" at work is actually extrapolation : extending a past trend forward on the assumption that the past pattern keeps holding.

articles.title: Apple Advancing API Support for Dual SIM Management
articles.excerpt: Apple has officially moved a developer request to the development phase (Phase III) that aims to expand API access for Dual SIM management on iPhone. This initiative, driven by EU interoperability req…
articles.body: Apple has officially moved a developer request to the development phase (Phase III) that aims to expand API access for Dual SIM management on iPhone. This initiative, driven by EU interoperability requirements under the Digital Markets Act (DMA), seeks to bridge the gap between first-party Phone/Contacts app capabilities and third-party developer access. What is changing Currently, developers building third-party calling or contact management apps are restricted from accessing specific cellular line metadata. The proposed changes would provide access to: Line Labels: Ability to read user-defined labels (e.g., "Work", "Personal") for each active SIM/eSIM. Contact Preferences: Ability to read and modify the preferred cellular line associated with specific contacts.

articles.body: A 25-minute interview script for founders, product engineers and PMs testing an AI product idea: recent behaviour, workarounds, trust, and what happens when the output is wrong. Good product discovery interview questions ask people to reconstruct a recent, real task: what triggered it, what they did, where it broke, what the workaround cost, and, for AI products, where they would accept automation and how they would check its output. They never start with "would you use an AI thatâ€¦". The script below runs in 25 minutes and ends with a commitment, not a compliment. Key takeaways Ask about the last time, not the usual time. Teresa Torres warns that general questions make people overestimate their habits because they forget the exceptions ( Product Talk ).

articles.excerpt: Copy the four product-market fit survey questions Superhuman used, send them to the right users, and score the answers by segment. Includes a template, sample-size table and worked example. A product-…
articles.body: Copy the four product-market fit survey questions Superhuman used, send them to the right users, and score the answers by segment. Includes a template, sample-size table and worked example. A product-market fit survey asks people who actively use your product one core question: "How would you feel if you could no longer use [product]?" If 40% or more answer "very disappointed", Sean Ellis's benchmark suggests you have product-market fit. Three follow-up questions tell you who those people are, what they value and what is holding everyone else back. Key takeaways The 40% benchmark comes from Sean Ellis comparing nearly a hundred startups: those that struggled almost always scored below 40%, those with strong traction almost always above ( First Round Review, 2018 ).

articles.title: Samsung could end annual Galaxy Watch releases starting in 2027
articles.excerpt: Fewer hardware launches could mean more time for meaningful upgrades.
articles.body: TL;DR Samsung reportedly plans to skip new Galaxy Watch models in 2027, breaking its annual release tradition. The move to a two-year launch cycle aims to reduce development and marketing costs. Samsung plans to focus on software updates and new health features for existing Galaxy Watches. Not every smartwatch needs a new model every year. Apple demonstrated that when it waited two years between the Watch Ultra 2 and Ultra 3, releasing only a new color in between. And with yearly hardware improvements becoming increasingly modest, there’s a growing debate over whether annual upgrades are still necessary. Samsung could now take things a step further by abandoning yearly Galaxy Watch releases altogether.

Google’s new Noto 3D emoji were supposed to give Android a fresh look, but their surprisingly demanding hardware requirements have left some users scratching their heads. After all, why should a new set of emoji require 6GB of RAM and 10GB of free storage? While Google’s support page also confirmed that Samsung phones won’t receive the new designs , the hardware requirements sparked another debate, prompting Google to step in with an explanation.
